spec: 0:00.0–0:05.3 "PHP just had a bug that could let a total stranger run code on your server."
board: Title scribble "PHP2Shell" fades in at the end

spec: 0:06.7–0:17.9 "PHP runs about 7 in 10 websites. On October 21st, it shipped an emergency fix. Two bugs, PHP2Shell, and I've spent like last 24 hours on just patching servers."

text: PHP is the engine under WordPress, Drupal, Magento and Laravel. Both bugs are rated 9.2 out of 10, and Amazon's honeypots saw an attack attempt on October 17th, four days before the fix.
board: logos as hand-lettered names around a PHP logo, "9.2" in red, Oct 17 → Oct 21 mini timeline

spec: 0:21.2–~0:29 "So how does it work? When you open a website, your browser sends a request. Think of it as a form. Your name, your email, and sometimes a file,"
0:32.6–0:39.4 "Before the website's own code even wakes up, PHP tries to unpack that into the memory."
board: cloud → server tower + PHP logo → green RAM stick (blue "allocate" arrow)

text: That form arrives as an HTTP POST. Before your code runs, PHP reads every field and builds it in RAM, keeping a little bookkeeping: how many slots it reserved and how many it has filled.

spec: 0:39.7–0:46.4 "Now picture this. Picture memory as a row of lockers. Gray is free and teal is in use."
board: RAM zooms into a row of lockers, grey vs teal

spec: 0:46.9–0:59.6 shaadi album, 400 photos, 4K, "har mama-mami ka photo"
1:00.4–1:19.3 "PHP needs 12 lockers … only memory for 10 … memory runs out halfway … 'sab ho gaya' … slide everything under the bed."
board: 10 lockers fill, 2 dashed ones; red "OUT OF MEMORY"; bed + junk doodle

spec: 1:32.5–1:40.6 "Lockers 11 and 12 are never filled. So they are just leftover junk. And PHP uses that junk as real data, right."
board: red stamp arrow on lockers 11–12, "junk → used as real"

text: Technically: PHP hits its memory limit while it's still building your form. The cleanup that runs next assumes the half-built data is complete, so it uses slots that were never set up. And the attacker gets to shape what sits in that junk.
board: "OOM" + "cleanup assumes done" annotations, red attacker figure

text: Bug two is a use-after-free. When a request finishes, PHP frees its locker for the next one. But some leftover state still points at it, like an old sticky note with a locker number. The next request on the same PHP worker moves into that locker, and PHP follows the old note straight to the attacker's data.
board: second locker row; yellow sticky note "→ 7"; red request moves in; arrow follows the note

text: Chain the two, and someone with no login can steer PHP into running their commands. A command line on your server. That's the 'shell' in PHP2Shell.

spec: 2:29.6–2:42.0 "if you really use this exploit, you can basically open up a Pandora box where people can connect to your servers… So it's very big. It's very serious."
2:42.5–2:46.7 "That's why we had to like wake up in the middle of the night and fix this at all cost."
2:46.9–2:54.0 "Now the good news: the public exploits so far don't work on default setup. They usually need a second bug in your app."

text: But the flaw itself is in every unpatched PHP since version 5.4, back in 2012. So don't wait for a better exploit to show up.

spec: 3:08.1–3:10.6 "So here's what you need to do. Update your PHP immediately."
3:15.4–3:23.0 "They were supposed to release on 22nd, but they released it on 21st… upgrade the version of PHP, restart your Apache, restart your PHP, and you're good to go."

text: Check with php dash v. The fixed versions are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. On 8.1 or older there's no official release, so upgrade or use your distro's patched package.

spec: 4:28.0–4:35.7 "…if you can't update the PHP, set the memory limit to minus one, that is one of the vendor's solutions."

text: The other stopgap is turning off session upload progress. Both are partial. Updating is the real fix.
board: "partial!" in red; "UPDATE = real fix" in green

text: One more thing. The researchers behind these finds say they used AI models to hunt for them. Expect bugs to be found faster, and patch windows to get shorter.

spec: 4:18.3–4:21.0 "There is nothing left in my eyes right now."

text: Patch first. Panic never. Save this for your next deploy.
